Verse logic for n bottles at start:
- n > 1: "{n} bottles of beer on the wall, {n} bottles of beer.\nTake one down and pass it around, {n-1} bottle(s) of beer on the wall."
- n == 1: "1 bottle of beer on the wall, 1 bottle of beer.\nTake it down and pass it around, no more bottles of beer on the wall."
- n == 0: "No more bottles of beer on the wall, no more bottles of beer.\nGo to the store and buy some more, 99 bottles of beer on the wall."

```python
def _verse(number):
    if number == 0:
        first = "No more bottles of beer on the wall, no more bottles of beer."
        second = "Go to the store and buy some more, 99 bottles of beer on the wall."
    else:
        quantity = "{} bottle{}".format(number, "" if number == 1 else "s")
        first = "{} of beer on the wall, {} of beer.".format(quantity, quantity)
        if number == 1:
            second = "Take it down and pass it around, no more bottles of beer on the wall."
        else:
            next_quantity = "{} bottle{}".format(number - 1, "" if number == 1 else "s")
            second = "Take one down and pass it around, {} of beer on the wall.".format(next_quantity)
    return [first, second]


def recite(start, take=1):
    verses = []
    for number in range(start, start - take, -1):
        verses.extend(_verse(number))
    return verses
```

```python
def _quantity(number):
    if number == 0:
        return "no more bottles"
    if number == 1:
        return "1 bottle"
    return f"{number} bottles"


def _verse(number):
    if number == 0:
        return [
            "No more bottles of beer on the wall, no more bottles of beer.",
            "Go to the store and buy some more, 99 bottles of beer on the wall.",
        ]
    action = "Take it down" if number == 1 else "Take one down"
    return [
        f"{_quantity(number).capitalize()} of beer on the wall, {_quantity(number)} of beer.",
        f"{action} and pass it around, {_quantity(number - 1)} of beer on the wall.",
    ]


def recite(start, take=1):
    lines = []
    for number in range(start, start - take, -1):
        if lines:
            lines.append("")
        lines.extend(_verse(number))
    return lines
```

Note: `_quantity(number).capitalize()` → "No more bottles" (capitalize lowercases rest but it's already fine: "no more bottles" → "No more bottles"). For number>0 quantities have no other capitals. Good.
